newsitem.title: CHINA: KONKA RISING SALES BOOST FIRST HALF NET.
newsitem.headline: KONKA RISING SALES BOOST FIRST HALF NET.

text.p: Rising sales and lower production costs helped to boost the first-half earnings of Chinese colour television maker Konka Group Co Ltd, a company spokesman said on Monday.

The company, China's second biggest colour television maker, on Saturday posted net profits of 164.60 million yuan for the first half of 1997, up 15.4 percent year-on-year under international accounting standards.
"Rising sales were the main factor in boosting our net profits," the spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Sales of the Shenzhen-based group totalled 2,373.01 million yuan in the first half, compared with 2,031.48 million yuan in the same period last year, he said.
The company turned out 1.34 million colour television sets in the first six months, up 38 percent year-on-year. Output included 670,000 sets produced by three of its subsidiaries.
Konka has acquired controlling stakes in four small television makers outside Shenzhen and the affiliates have started producing Konka-brand televisions, the spokesman said.
"Relatively lower production costs at those affiliates also helped to lift our net profits," he said.
The official said the company would mainly rely on promotions rather than price cuts to boost sales in the second half.
Konka rode out a cut-throat price war among Chinese television makers last year, boosting its market share to 13 percent in 1996 from nine percent in the previous year.
The company expected a stronger performance in the second half due to seasonal factors, the spokesman said, adding that television sales usually increased in the latter part of the year.
As of the end of June, the company had 366 million outstanding shares, including 79 million domestic A shares, 48 million hard currency B shares and about 238 million non-tradeable shares.
Its per share net reached 0.45 yuan in the first half with assets per share at 4.42 yuan.
